q: 1. Two projects having the same status expect payback period which project will be selected?
options: The project having more payback period
The project having less payback period
All off all of the above
explain: If everything else is equal, the project that recovers its investment sooner (shorter payback period) is preferred because it carries less risk and returns cash faster.

q: 2. The number of year from commissioning of the project at which net operating benefit equals to the investment is called ......
explain: Payback period is the time, counted from commissioning, after which cumulative net operating benefit equals the investment.

q: 3. The number of years required for the net operating benefit to pay back the initial cost of project is called ......
explain: This is the definition of payback period: years needed for net operating benefits to recover the initial cost.

q: 4. Pay Back period is counted only after ......
options: starting of the construction of a project
completion of the construction of project
explain: Benefits begin only when the project is commissioned, so the payback period is counted from commissioning, not from tendering or construction.

q: 5. For the selection of a project B/C ratio should be ......
explain: A project is acceptable when present worth of benefits exceeds present worth of costs, i.e. B/C > 1.

q: 6. In a project selection, minimum B/C ratio should be ......
explain: The minimum (threshold) B/C ratio is 1, where benefits just equal costs. Note: strictly, B/C above 1 is preferred; the key gives the threshold value.

q: 7. The minimum value of benefit cost ratio for selection of any project should ...... for acceptation of project.
explain: The minimum acceptable B/C ratio is equal to 1 (break-even). Below 1 the project is rejected. Note: this is the same idea as Q8; the key marks b.

q: 8. Which one of the following statements in correct?
options: The number of years required to recover the initial cash investment in a project, is called Pay Back Period (PBP)
The discount rate that equates the present value of the expected Net Cash Flows (CFS) with the Initial Cash Outflow (ICO) is known as internal rate of return
The present value of the proposal's net cash flows, less the proposal's initial cash outflow is known as the Net Present Value (NPV)
explain: All three statements correctly define standard project-evaluation metrics: Payback Period, Internal Rate of Return, and Net Present Value.

q: 9. For the selection of any project the NPV should be ......
explain: A project is acceptable if NPV is zero or more; the minimum acceptable NPV is 0. A negative NPV is rejected, so option b cannot be right.

q: 10. If NPV is +ve then, NFV is ......
explain: NFV = NPV x (1+i)^n, and (1+i)^n is always positive, so NFV has the same sign as NPV.

q: 11. The difference of discounted benefit and cost is called ......
explain: NPV = present value of benefits minus present value of costs.

q: 12. Two projects having same status except pay back period. Which project will be selected?
options: the project having more pay back period
the project having less pay back period
explain: A shorter payback period is preferred as it recovers the initial investment faster.

q: 13. The number of years required for the net operating benefits to payback the initial cost of the project is called
explain: This is the formal definition of the Payback Period.

q: 14. As the present worth of the project increases the project becomes more feasible ......
explain: Higher present worth means greater net economic gain, so the project is more feasible economically.

q: 15. Pay back period is counted only after
options: starting of the construction of the project
completion of the construction of the project
explain: Recovery of costs begins once the project is operational and generates revenue (commissioning).

q: 16. For the selection of any project minimum future worth should be ......
explain: Future worth must be zero or positive for acceptance, so the minimum is 0.

q: 17. Benefit cost ratio is the ratio of
explain: The B/C ratio compares the Present Value of Benefits to the Present Value of Costs.

q: 18. Project is assumed as feasible if ......
options: IRR is greater than borrow rate
IRR is lesser than borrow rate
IRR is equal to borrow rate
explain: A project is feasible when its IRR exceeds the cost of borrowing.

q: 19. For the selection of a project B/C ratio should be
explain: A project is viable if benefits exceed costs, i.e., the ratio is greater than 1.

q: 20. At what condition project is good ......
options: IRR equal to the discount rate
explain: If IRR is greater than the discount rate, NPV at that discount rate is positive, so the project is good.

q: 21. The benefit cost ratio is
options: no any relation with discount rate
explain: As the discount rate increases, the present value of future benefits decreases more significantly than initial costs, lowering the B/C ratio.

q: 22. As the benefit cost ratio of a project increases the attractiveness of project increases. But minimum value should be... for acception.
explain: While higher is better, the absolute minimum for acceptance is parity (1.0).

q: 23. The ratio of discounted benefit and discounted cost is called
explain: This defines the Benefit-Cost ratio.

q: 24. In a project selection, minimum B/C ratio should be
explain: The decision threshold is exactly 1.

q: 25. For the selection of any project which criteria is followed ......
explain: IRR, NPV and B/C ratio are all standard criteria for project selection.

q: 26. For the selection of any project which one is mostly used ......
explain: The key marks IRR as the most widely used criterion. Note: many textbooks name NPV; follow the key.

q: 27. Two projects having same status except payback period which Project will be selected?
options: the project having more payback period
the project having less payback period
explain: A shorter payback period is preferred because it recovers the initial investment faster, reducing risk and exposure.

q: 28. For the analysis of any project net present value may be ......
explain: During analysis NPV can come out positive, zero or negative; the sign then decides acceptance.

q: 29. The number of years required for the net operating benefits to payback the initial cost of the project is called
explain: This is the definition of the payback period — the time needed for net benefits to equal the initial investment.

q: 30. For selection of the project net present value should be ......
explain: A project is selected when its NPV is positive, meaning benefits exceed costs.

q: 31. During analysis of any project, numerical value of net present worth is found negative then, internal rate of return should be ......
explain: A negative NPW at a trial rate means the IRR is lower than that rate, so a lower discount rate must be tried. The key marks a.

q: 32. Benefit cost ratio is the ratio of
explain: Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR) is defined as the Present Value of Benefits divided by the Present Value of Costs: PVB/PVC.

q: 33. In a project selection ERR should be ......
explain: The key marks ERR > 0 (a positive external rate of return) as the condition for selection.

q: 34. For accepting of project, the minimum value of benefit cost ratio should be
explain: For a project to be minimally acceptable, BCR must be at least equal to one (benefits at least cover costs).

q: 35. For the selection of any project the NPV should be
explain: None of the given options (zero or less than zero) represent the typical 'selection' criteria, which is NPV > 0.

q: 36. Net present value is defined as total present value of ...... of cash flows.
explain: NPV is the total present value of the net amount (benefits minus costs) of cash flows.

q: 37. MARR (Marginal Annual Rate of Return) is
explain: MARR is the minimum acceptable return an investor expects after committing capital.

q: 38. The numerical value of MARR is
explain: For a project to be accepted, the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) must exceed the MARR.

q: 39. The difference of discounted benefit and cost is called
explain: Net Present Value is $PV(Benefits) - PV(Costs)$.

q: 40. For the selection of any project the NPV should be
explain: Per the answer key, the minimum acceptable NPV threshold for project selection is zero (NPV ≥ 0 indicates the project is at least break-even in present value terms).

q: 41. MARR (Marginal annual rate of return) is
explain: MARR represents the minimum acceptable rate of return expected as benefit resulting after an investment is made (note: options a and b are printed identically in the source book).

q: 42. Find the NPV if initial investment 5,000, Benefit for three years = 3000 per year and discount rate = 9%.
43. The benefit cost ratio is ......
options: superior to all of the above method
explain: A higher discount rate lowers the present worth of future benefits more than costs, so B/C falls as the discount rate rises.

q: 44. For any project to be feasible ......
options: annual worth should be equal to zero
payback period should be equal to or less than 5 year
explain: A project is feasible when its present worth is positive.

q: 45. Net present value is a term widely used in ......
explain: The key marks project cost analysis (c): NPV is a term used in project cost-benefit evaluation.

q: 46. The minimum NPV for selection of any project should be
explain: A project is considered financially acceptable if its Net Present Value (NPV) is at least zero, meaning it meets the required rate of return.

q: 47. During analysis of projects following NPV is obtained -1, 0, 0.5 and 1. Which project should be selected economically considering the maximum benefit?
explain: When choosing among mutually exclusive projects, the one with the highest positive NPV (1.0 in this case) provides the most value.

q: 48. The discount rate that makes the net present value equal to zero is known as ......
explain: IRR is the discount rate at which NPV = 0.

q: 49. During analysis of projects following NPV is obtained -1, 0, 0.5 and 1. Which project should be confirmly rejected?
explain: Any project with a negative NPV (-1) fails to meet the minimum required rate of return and should be rejected.

q: 50. In what case, protect is feasible?
explain: Economic feasibility is established when the Present Worth (PW) of benefits exceeds the costs, resulting in a value greater than zero.
